video.title: She Makes $40K/Month with This Weird Hawaiian Dessert

summary: UpFlip visits Get Lost Shaved Ice in Virginia Beach, a Hawaiian shave ice shop opened in October 2023 by Stephanie and her husband Todd after a Hawaii honeymoon. They spent eight to nine months on recipe R&D, make about 10 dye-free syrups from scratch every Monday, sell $9.50-13.50 bowls with an estimated goods cost of cents per syrup portion, and run a food truck in summer (about 15% of revenue). 2025 revenue was $408.5k with a best month of about $95k, but after labour ($114k), rent ($50k+), $65k owner pay and other costs, net was about $23.5k; merch is claimed at about 20% of revenue at 50-60% margins. Lessons: the business is extremely seasonal and labour-heavy (3-4 staff in winter, 25 in summer), the buildout doubled from $60k, health department approval was hard, and a non-literal brand name enabled merch.

ideas.problem: No authentic Hawaiian shave ice locally; people want dye-free, preservative-free desserts

unit_economics_claims: COGS $79.5k, labour ~$114k, card fees $14k, rent $50k+, payroll tax $15k, repairs $10k, interest $3k, merch COGS $23k

acquisition.how: Social media and influencer invites can be partly automated; walk-in trade depends on location.

delivery.how: Handmade food prep and service by up to 25 seasonal staff.

uk_applicability.notes: UK climate makes it even more seasonal; needs council food registration, hygiene rating, and street trading licences for trucks/carts. Labour-intensive, not automatable.

risks: Labour churn and retraining each summer
Health department and food truck regulations

tactics.name: Free product for local micro-creators
steps: Find content creators with concentrated local followings
Invite them for free product rather than paying
Let first-time reactions ('life changing') drive word of mouth

quote.text: finding content creators within your field
quote.speaker: Stephanie

tactics.name: Pick a brand name that sells merch
steps: Choose a name unrelated to the product (Get Lost) that people want to wear
Sell sweatshirts, tees, tanks for kids and adults in an on-site merch shed
Merch earns 50-60% margin with no labour per unit

quote.text: No one wants to wear Virginia Beach Shave Ice or a T-shirt, right

tactics.name: Start simple, then expand the menu

warnings.warning: Food trucks face location time limits; a fixed truck with seating was not allowed.

quote.text: We quickly found out that the regulations were completely against that you cannot do that
quote.speaker: Stephanie

warnings.warning: Health inspectors resisted a new concept (making own ice blocks and syrups); expect many 'no's.

quote.text: We had a lot of stumbling blocks being told no a lot of different times
quote.speaker: Stephanie

warnings.warning: Seasonality is extreme: sales drop the day kids return to school, winters are dismal.

quote.text: The day kids go back to school. It is over
quote.speaker: Stephanie

warnings.warning: Despite $408k revenue, net was only ~$23.5k; labour is the biggest line item.
Seasonal staff mostly don't return, so you retrain every year.
Using life savings and personal loans was terrifying; debt still being repaid.

lessons.lesson: Bring a product you discover while travelling to a market that doesn't have it.
Quality, scratch-made ingredients and branding justify premium prices.

quote.text: I think quality product and branding
quote.speaker: Todd

lessons.lesson: High-margin merch can subsidise a labour-heavy core product.

quote.text: you sell a $60 sweatshirt. You've got to sell six shavers
quote.speaker: Todd

lessons.lesson: Test cheaply (cart or truck) before committing to a brick-and-mortar buildout.

quote.text: a food truck is definitely a lower cost of entry than a brick and mortar and a full build out
quote.speaker: Stephanie

lessons.lesson: Revenue is not profit; seasonal food businesses can have high sales and thin margins.
Flexibility and calm problem solving are core owner skills; something breaks every day.

quote.text: There's always gonna be a problem. Every single day there's a problem
quote.speaker: Stephanie

lessons.lesson: Year-round warm markets (Florida) remove the seasonality problem for weather-dependent products.
Keeping ownership (no investors) means self-funding risk.

evidence_quality.rationale: First-hand owners sharing a P&L with specific figures, though some line items are approximate and the Whisper transcript garbles words.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Sponsor read for Busy; UpFlip promotes its assessment tool.

extraction.review_notes: The extraction is thorough and accurate on the P&L figures, prices, staffing, seasonality and startup costs, and its evidence and promotion flags are reasonable. The main gaps were a missing special-tier price point and a merch revenue-share claim that was folded into the margin claim instead of standing alone. Some figures are inconsistent and only approximate. The headline '$40k/month' is above the implied average of about $34k/month from $408.5k a year. Store 85%, truck 15% and merch about 20% do not add up, and the host admits the line items do not reconcile. An A rating is borderline; B would also be defensible.
